title: Acute-event health and bill context differs by coverage group, but not uniformly
source_unit: MEPS 2024 under-65 person records grouped by INSURC24 coverage and annual presence of an emergency-room, inpatient, or office event

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; under-65 coverage-conditioned event presence and same-year context

denominator.unit: under-65 HC-256 person records across private, public-only, and uninsured coverage groups; event and outcome denominators are cell-specific

observations.method: Classify annual event presence from HC-254A/254D/254E/254G event files, append under-65 INSURC24 coverage from HC-256 by DUPERSID and PANEL, and calculate person-weighted context shares using PERWT24F with standard BRR across 128 replicate flags.
observations.uncertainty: These are same-year descriptive associations, not insurance effects or event-triggered burden estimates. Event presence reflects need, severity, access, utilization, and selection; the no-event group is not a no-need control. The uninsured inpatient cell has 16 valid records and is omitted from promoted comparisons.
observations.subgroup: Under-65 private, public-only, and uninsured coverage groups; separate office, emergency-room, and inpatient event universes with outcome-specific valid denominators.
observations.counterinterpretation: The private-insurance office-event bill-problem shares are nearly identical (7.29% versus 7.03%) despite a health difference, showing that utilization, health status, and reported payment difficulty do not form one universal burden gradient.

related_sources.claim: The method note documents the coverage-conditioned event comparison, selected counterexample, and open episode fields.
The machine output preserves all coverage/event cells, standard errors, and valid counts.

reproduction_audit.inputs: HC-256, HC-036BRR, and HC-254A/254D/254E/254G local artifacts
reproduction_audit.result: The committed local machine output contains coverage-conditioned person-weighted shares and standard-BRR uncertainty; raw archives remain outside the repository.

boundary: This layer places coverage and observed event presence beside same-year health and bill-problem context. It does not identify a dated bill, care alternative, delayed or foregone care, borrowing, unpaid time, treatment continuity, remedy, recovery, trust, switching, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
